title: Investigate the user, job and value of a quote-to-job prototype

observations.quote: Clients can also request changes online and pay a deposit using Jobber Payments while approving the quote.
observations.statement: Vendor documentation advertises changes and deposits during approval. This is not evidence of demand for another tool.

observations.quote: However once a quote has been converted to a job, any updates made to the quote do not appear on the job.
observations.statement: Jobber documents non-propagation of later quote edits. This is not a runtime observation or a complete versioning specification.

observations.quote: You can quickly convert an estimate into a job in Housecall Pro, carrying over all relevant details without re-entering information.
observations.statement: Vendor advertises conversion without re-entry; transferred fields, actual speed and reliability are not established by this excerpt.

observations.quote: With Square Invoices Plus, you can auto-convert an estimate to an invoice once your customer accepts your estimate.
observations.statement: Square advertises acceptance-triggered estimate-to-invoice conversion on Invoices Plus. An invoice is not necessarily an operational job record; pricing and broader job behavior are unknown here.

observations.quote: Using a template saves time by providing a pre-formatted structure with built-in formulas.
observations.statement: Microsoft advertises formula-based templates and asserts time savings. Templates are a credible baseline capability; savings for this operator have not been measured.

observations.quote: Note: Quote imports create new quotes only. Existing quotes cannot be edited through a CSV import.
observations.statement: Jobber documents quote creation by CSV, but not updating existing quotes by import. This rebuts a blanket no-import claim and identifies an update constraint, not an automatic switching advantage.

observations.quote: We want to stop this as it’s no longer sustainable for us to run around the city just to do quotes
observations.statement: One unverified public report objects to travel for quoting. It suggests an intake/scoping problem, not proof that quote-to-job tracking removes visits. The poster is not a verified buyer or lead.

observations.quote: All my scheduling is done on Apple Calendar. I write reports on Apple Numbers. I send invoices from Quickbooks.
observations.statement: One unverified report describes a calendar/spreadsheet/accounting stack. This challenges assuming everyone needs an integrated replacement; satisfaction, performance and prevalence are not established.

observations.quote: I know for a fact that we are double and triple entering information on our different platforms
observations.statement: One unverified poster reports repeated entry. This motivates a handoff-friction hypothesis but does not establish cause, frequency, cost, switching intent or small-operator fit.

observations.quote: Available supplied assets are existing MIDAS software, a laptop, current development tools and willingness to learn. School, sleep and existing commitments constrain availability. No buyer network or industry expertise is confirmed. Founder effort, commercial budget, customer demand and business results remain unmeasured.
observations.statement: Assistant restatement of owner-supplied context, not a verbatim founder quote or independent verification. Assets and constraints are reported; access and delivery capacity are not demonstrated. This source confers no new authority.

recommendation.title: Bounded engineering experiment; no commercial switching recommendation
recommendation.basis:
Decision. Recommend the separately authorized quote-to-job-v2 experiment to answer whether MIDAS can support reliable local quote editing, same-record job-status handoff and persistent retrieval. That unresolved execution question serves the stated prototype goal; availability of a profile alone is not the reason to build. Retain a competent existing process for real operations. Neither a commercial launch nor customer switching is justified. This task delivers research, not application software.

Evidence method. The supplied exact excerpts suffice for this bounded decision: vendor documentation establishes advertised capabilities, public reports are unverified examples, and founder context is an attributed assistant restatement. Broader source interpretations are not additional observed facts. Another vendor search would not resolve actual operator access, workflow performance or implementation behavior, so no additional retrieval is needed.

1. Who would use this? Candidate, not confirmed segment: a small service owner-operator or office coordinator who creates itemized quotes and personally tracks the subsequent work, potentially re-entering details between tools. public-repeat-entry motivates that hypothesis but does not confirm its prevalence or fit. Users whose primary needs are crew dispatch, customer approval, payments or accounting may be better served by existing products. No participating operator, buyer network or founder industry expertise is confirmed (founder-capacity).

2. What exact job would it improve? Proposed job: enter a customer and priced line items, save and reopen the quote, edit without duplicating it, mark it scheduled, track progress and recover saved details later. A single saved record could avoid a quote-to-tracker copying step; this is a causal hypothesis, not measured improvement. Correction to the inherited draft: the supplied profile changes the status of one record. It has no approval event, accepted-version linkage, independent job snapshot, location field or appointment time. Scheduled is a status, not calendar scheduling. It cannot establish client consent or preserve a frozen agreed scope. public-quote-travel concerns obtaining scope for a quote; this tracker does not establish remote scoping, correct prices or fewer visits.

3. What do they use today? The target operator's actual process is unknown. A competent designed baseline is a validated spreadsheet with stable record IDs, itemized formulas, controlled edits and status tracking, plus a linked calendar for appointments, accounting software for invoices and a backup routine. Microsoft supports the template/formula capability (spreadsheet-template); public-existing-stack describes a related combination. Do not compare against an artificially broken sheet. Jobber advertises approval changes/deposits, conversion with no propagation of later quote edits, and CSV creation of quotes (jobber-approval, jobber-handoff, jobber-import). Housecall Pro advertises conversion without re-entry (housecall-conversion). Square Invoices Plus advertises accepted-estimate conversion to invoices (square-invoice), potentially enough when billing is the real endpoint. These excerpts do not establish prices, full feature coverage, actual usability or portability. Improving the baseline, using an incumbent, or stopping are credible alternatives.

4. What specific advantage could justify switching? Conditional hypothesis: for an operator with a narrow, recurring copying problem, one local record and explicit status controls might reduce handoff steps with little setup and no new service account. Neither that setup advantage nor demand for local-only operation is demonstrated; do not infer that competitors lack offline options. Conversion itself is not differentiated. Jobber's create-only import is a constraint, but CSV ingestion also weakens an alleged import moat. A switch would require observed recurring friction and a relevant fit advantage over the competent baseline or incumbent, sufficient to outweigh migration, training, backup responsibilities and lost features. No labor savings, pricing advantage or specialist superiority is established.

5. How could we reach them? Unvalidated future routes are owner-provided introductions, local trade/supplier introductions, or moderator-approved workflow research in a relevant operator community. Founder access, channel effectiveness and acquisition cost are unknown. Under separate outreach authority and participant consent, observe a recent anonymized quote, revision and handoff in the person's actual tools; record what works and reasons not to switch. Public posters are examples, not leads. No messages, accounts, purchases or commitments are executed here. Interviews are not a prerequisite for the synthetic local engineering experiment; they would be needed to strengthen a commercial user/advantage hypothesis.

6. Which assumptions are supported, contradicted or unknown? Supported only at the stated evidence level: advertised conversion/import/template capabilities; individual reports of repeated entry, travel frustration and a multi-tool stack; reported founder tools and availability constraints. Contradicted at the advertised-capability level: conversion is novel or missing, and incumbents cannot import spreadsheet quotes. Challenged, not population-tested: every fragmented stack needs replacement, and a handoff tracker fixes travel-based quoting. Unknown: recurring error frequency and causes, adequacy of the competent baseline, preferred revision practices, switching tolerance, real user access, founder available hours and implementation capability, and comparative setup burden. Reported assets are not measured delivery capacity. Cost and revenue remain unobserved in USD; no demand, margin, willingness to pay or SaaS opportunity is inferred.

7. What would building let us learn or accomplish? Named question: can the supported MIDAS bridge and UI maintain correct itemized totals and stable record identity through editing, job-status changes and persistent retrieval, while visibly rejecting invalid input or failed saves? A successful bounded implementation would perform that local tracking job, not validate a business. Use only the supplied quote-to-job-v2 contract: app.html with inline CSS/JavaScript, no network/assets/accounts, initially empty with synthetic data entered explicitly, bounded integer quantities and integer-cent USD arithmetic. The bridge getState/saveState with expectedVersion is authoritative; never claim a save before success or use localStorage as authoritative state. Preserve stable IDs and all earlier records when creating another. Conversion changes quoted to scheduled on the same record, followed by in_progress/completed; do not implement the inherited approval/snapshot workflow.

Concrete fixture: 2 x $75.00 + 3 x $20.00 = $210.00 (21000 cents). Reopen and change the $75.00 rate to $90.00: $240.00 (24000 cents), same ID, no duplicate. Add a second quote without losing the first; convert and progress the first record. Check saved customers, lines, totals and statuses after refresh, a fresh preview session and a host restart using the same data directory. The old $210.00 is not a retained approval or frozen job snapshot. Run the fixed build journey unchanged, including invalid/blank inputs without mutation, rejection of extra price precision, visible save errors, 1280px/390px usability, and all-record CSV export with numeric two-decimal totals, escaping and formula guards. CSV is a local export, not an invoice or sent offer. Compare identical applicable cases with the competent baseline, retaining actual failures and actions rather than simulated competence or projected time savings.

A pass would support only the exercised revision's behavior under recorded conditions. It would not establish long-term durability, device-loss recovery, production security, multi-user/device behavior, legal acceptance, tax/deposit/payment correctness, real calendar scheduling, integrations, remote scoping, demand or superiority. If the execution question has no value, capacity is unavailable, or required work exceeds the existing authority/profile, defer or stop rather than expand scope. No new interview or commercial approval is required merely to finish this report.

Artifact and delivery evidence. At correction intake the sole supplied file was the preserved 20542-byte brief.json, SHA-256 6290519b4366f4f6f6d25cd221d59346e71c22f208b3b75a55e86cbb95f39847. Four size-rejected writes (20447, 19148, 19240 and 18473 bytes) left it unchanged. No application source/runtime observation or successful current report-check/publication receipt was supplied. This correction removes the unsupported snapshot recommendation and shortens the report. Pair the corrected revision with actual check.run delivery.current output and artifact.publish_local delivery/readback evidence; the document does not self-certify a pass. Report delivery checks do not test the prospective application. Owner/customer acceptance, independent semantic review and independent correction time remain unknown.

steps.owner: Developer under the separately authorized build task; capacity unconfirmed
steps.action: Next, if its existing authority and capacity apply, execute quote-desk/build-v4-r1 using quote-to-job-v2, not a new approval/snapshot design. Record effort within existing limits and use the two-line fixture. No operator interview is a prerequisite.
steps.successMeasure: A scoped attempt addresses same-record editing, status handoff and persistence, or records a specific capacity/authority/value stop. No commercial claims or scope expansion.

steps.action: Retain source and actual browser/bridge evidence; inspect defects, repair, rerun unchanged required build checks and publish locally. Exercise the supported persistence boundaries and preserve unsupported cases.
steps.successMeasure: Manifest-bound results and local delivery/readback show the exercised behavior, including $210.00 to $240.00 editing without duplication and preservation of both records. Failures are reported, not waived.

steps.action: Compare the implemented prototype, if any, with the competent baseline on identical applicable cases. Record setup burden, errors, omissions and actual effort; choose keep, repair or stop. Prefer the baseline or an incumbent where better suited.
steps.successMeasure: A decision separates demonstrated local behavior from hypotheses. Synthetic action counts are not reported as labor savings; independent review and acceptance stay unknown unless recorded.

steps.owner: Owner/researcher, only with separate outreach authority and consent
steps.action: Only if commercial investigation remains worthwhile, establish legitimate access and observe an anonymized current workflow, including revisions and reasons not to switch. Otherwise preserve the access gap without sending anything.
steps.successMeasure: A consented workflow account or explicit access limitation is retained. One account is not prevalence, demand or willingness-to-pay validation.

unknowns: Actual operator access, workflow volume, recurring handoff errors, causes and adequacy of the current process are unobserved.
Founder available hours, implementation skills, budget and opportunity cost are unmeasured; tools and willingness do not establish capacity.
No application behavior has been observed here. Persistence, recovery, usability and comparative setup burden await an authorized implementation.
Vendor prices, complete workflows and actual performance are not established by the excerpts; public reports are not representative evidence.
Cost and revenue in USD, demand, acquisition effectiveness, willingness to switch/pay, retention, labor savings and specialist superiority remain unknown.
Owner/customer acceptance, independent semantic review and independent correction time remain unknown until directly recorded.

obligations.description: Any build must follow quote-to-job-v2 and its own authority/limits. Preserve actual source, unchanged check results, persistence observations, defects and local delivery/readback. This report is not software evidence.
Before outreach, establish authority and consent. Observe the real baseline, recurring problem or its absence, and switching constraints. Do not treat public posters as leads or infer founder access.

obligations.owner: Independent reviewer and owner/customer, if available
obligations.description: Review all seven answers, source fidelity, profile limits and actual delivered-revision receipts. Record corrections/time when observed. Local publication is neither independent semantic approval nor customer acceptance and executes no messages or commitments.

Before commercial positioning, establish a defensible user/advantage hypothesis, reachable participants, available effort and observed economics. Keep demand, cost and revenue unobserved until supported; prefer a baseline/incumbent or stop when warranted.
